htn_kidney.title: Nephrinuria as a marker of podocyte dysfunction in hypertensive nephropathy: relationship with renal functional reserve and changes during renin-angiotensin system blockade.
htn_kidney.authors: Zokirov V, Tillakobilov I, Isroilov I

htn_kidney.abstract: Hypertensive kidney injury is often detected late by conventional markers. Urinary nephrin excretion (nephrinuria) reflects podocyte injury and may help identify renal involvement in essential hypertension. In this prospective, single-centre study, 60 adults with essential hypertension (20 per 2018 ESC/ESH stage, I-III; 20 men, 40 women) were assessed at baseline and after 6 months of antihypertensive treatment based on renin-angiotensin system (RAS) blockade (enalapril, n = 17; azilsartan, n = 43; add-on eplerenone, n = 21).
